figures.finding: Guyana has no performer's permit: no child (a person under fifteen) may be admitted to employment or work in any occupation, and the Act's schedule, which sets out the ILO Minimum Age Convention it implements, stops at Article 6, so the Convention's permits for artistic performances (Article 8) are not part of the law. From fifteen a young person is only kept from night work in industry (under sixteen) and the Chief Labour Officer enforces the Act. The bar on any occupation reaches a young writer or director as well.
figures.applies: Laws of Guyana revised to L.R.O. 1/2012.

sources.said: “child” means a person under the age of fifteen years; … 3. (1) No child shall be admitted to employment or work in any occupation. (2) No young person shall be employed at night in any industrial undertaking,

figures.finding: An infant's contracts for money lent or goods (other than necessaries) are absolutely void, others stand as the common law and equity allow, and a promise or ratification made after full age can't be sued on; no statute or court procedure for approving a minor's creative or performing contract, and no set-aside of earnings, was found.

value.binding: common law (Infancy Act s. 2 leaves other contracts to it); no court-approval procedure found
